title: Adaptive Closed-Loop Cognitive Intervention Protocols: A Multi-Center Randomized Trial
authors: Evelyn Vance, Marcus Sterling, H. R. Okafor

objective.gold_text: Evaluate whether dynamic stimulus-difficulty adaptation improves 12-week protocol retention compared to matched static difficulty in adults with mild cognitive impairment.
objective.gold_excerpt: The primary objective of this trial was to formally evaluate whether closed-loop cognitive load adaptation produces superior 12-week adherence compared to standard non-titrated clinical software regimes.

methodology.gold_text: Double-blind, multicenter randomized controlled trial with 1:1 allocation to active closed-loop titration vs fixed linear difficulty over 12 weeks.
methodology.gold_excerpt: 480 eligible adults... allocated 1:1 into two arms: Arm A (closed-loop automated titration, n=240) and Arm B (fixed linear difficulty progression, n=240).

population.gold_text: 480 adults aged 18-65 with diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22-25; 54.2% female, 45.8% male) across four academic health centers.
population.gold_excerpt: 480 eligible adults (mean age 54.2 ± 8.1 years; 54.2% female, 45.8% male) with confirmed early Mild Cognitive Impairment (MoCA 22–25)...

findings.gold_text: Adaptive cohort achieved 92.4% retention vs 78.1% in static arm (OR=3.14, 95% CI [1.81, 5.44], p<0.001). Cognitive fatigue reduction significant only in baseline severe fatigue subgroup.
findings.gold_excerpt: participants in the adaptive closed-loop cohort achieved a 92.4% retention rate (222/240) at week 12, compared to 78.1% (187/240) in the static control group (Odds Ratio = 3.14, p < 0.001).

limitations.unavailable_reason: Authors omitted drop-out survival curves, long-term persistence beyond 12 weeks, and adverse headache logs.
limitations.gold_excerpt: Several key parameters were uncollected in this trial: long-term persistence beyond 12 weeks was not assessed, and adverse sensory complaints such as migraine or tension headache occurrences were not monitored or recorded in participant journals.

ground_truth_qa_pairs.question: What was the 12-week retention rate in the adaptive arm versus control?
ground_truth_qa_pairs.expected_answer_summary: Adaptive arm achieved 92.4% (222/240) vs 78.1% (187/240) in control, OR 3.14.

expected_claims.claim_text: The adaptive protocol achieved 92.4% 12-week retention compared to 78.1% in static controls (p < 0.001).

gold_citations.verbatim_excerpt: In the intention-to-treat analysis, participants in the adaptive closed-loop cohort achieved a 92.4% retention rate (222/240) at week 12, compared to 78.1% (187/240) in the static control group (Odds Ratio = 3.14, 95% Confidence Interval [1.81, 5.44], p < 0.001).

ground_truth_qa_pairs.question: Did all participants experience statistically significant cognitive fatigue reduction?
ground_truth_qa_pairs.expected_answer_summary: No, fatigue reduction was only statistically significant in patients with baseline severe fatigue (VAS-F > 65); unstratified cohort showed non-significant difference.

expected_claims.claim_text: Cognitive fatigue reduction was statistically significant only in the severe baseline subgroup, and non-significant cohort-wide.

gold_citations.verbatim_excerpt: Secondary analyses showed a statistically significant reduction in post-session cognitive fatigue only among participants with baseline severe fatigue (VAS-F baseline > 65, adjusted difference -14.2 points, p = 0.021). For the overall cohort without elevated baseline fatigue, the between-group difference in fatigue was non-significant (p = 0.18).

ground_truth_qa_pairs.question: What was the 1-year economic cost-effectiveness per quality-adjusted life year (QALY)?
ground_truth_qa_pairs.expected_answer_summary: The authorized document lacks sufficient evidence: the study terminated at 12 weeks and collected no economic or QALY data.
